prompt: Thumbnail requests in ./%s are slow under load. The gallery service runs on 8 CPUs with one goroutine per request, and every request calls AverageColor on the *image.RGBA our resizer produces. Make it faster without changing its results or its exported API.
note: Each pixel goes through image.Image.At, an interface call that boxes a color.RGBA (65,536 allocs/op). Summing *image.RGBA's Pix row by row (PixOffset for a sub-image's Min and Stride) and scaling the sums by 257 to the 16 bits RGBA() reports is -92% sec/op. Traps: averaging the 8-bit values and widening the result rounds differently (the golden test's three-pixel case); a fast path that drops the At loop breaks the NRGBA, Gray and YCbCr cases; fanning rows out to goroutines is faster in a one-call benchmark and noisy on the golden RunParallel benchmark, where every CPU already serves a request. ParseHex uses fmt.Sscanf and runs once at startup.
